inputs.text: An Indiana judge blocked a pro-life law earlier this month after the ACLU and Hoosier Jews for Choice argued that limiting abortion burdens religious freedom. That turns a fundamental liberty into a weapon against the law’s duty to protect unborn life. Religious conscience matters, but it cannot be treated as a blank check to override the most vulnerable. When courts put abortion claims first, they erode the moral order that holds society together.

output.main_topic: An Indiana judge blocked a pro-life law after a religious-freedom challenge, prompting an argument against prioritizing abortion claims over protection of unborn life.
subtopics: Religious freedom arguments against abortion limits
